Subject: Post-call TCO recap & next steps (NovaHealth)

Hi Dana / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps. Notes below are intended to be brief; I attached a simple TCO workbook (redwood_tco_modeling.xlsx) that Ben and Rafael will flesh out with the numbers we discussed.

Attendees
- Dana Ellis (NovaHealth)
- Tom Berger (NovaHealth)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Ben Carter (Redwood) — pricing
- Rafael Mendes (Redwood) — infra/arch

Primary pain points
- Inference spend is spiking unpredictably during peak periods; current vendor invoices are hard to forecast.
- P95 latency concerns on 2k token prompts impacting clinician UX.
- Team needs to hit a hard budget target for POC/initial rollout: ~$10k/month.

Goals & success criteria
- Predictable monthly inference cost within your budget envelope (~$10k/mo for POC).
- Maintain P95 latency under 200ms for the majority of calls; degrade gracefully on tails.
- Clear path to scale while keeping unit economics stable.

Key cost levers we discussed
- Batching & request coalescing: for high-concurrency workloads we can reduce per-token overhead.
- KV/prefix caching: reuse repeated context to avoid re-computing early layers.
- Model selection & quantization: small/quantized variants for lower-cost paths for bulk workloads.
- Reserved/dedicated capacity: predictable unit rates and priority latency at scale.

Back-of-envelope TCO examples (to be validated in workbook)
- Example baseline (no batching/cache): 1M prompts/mo * ~600 tokens avg = ~600M tokens/mo -> current provider estimate: ~$18,000/mo.
- With batching + KV caching (expected 40–55% token compute reduction) -> estimated: $7,800–$10,800/mo.
- Reserved capacity + quantized model option could further reduce unit cost by ~15–25% at commit levels.

Immediate next steps
1) Ben to share an initial filled TCO workbook (assumptions + ranges) — ETA: EOD today.
2) Rafael to schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) to validate latency/kv-cache integration — target: next week.
3) NovaHealth to share target procurement timeline (you mentioned end of June) and any compliance docs needed.
4) Marissa to provide a concise 1–2 line ROI point for your exec brief.

Attachments: redwood_tco_modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains placeholders for prompts-per-month, avg tokens, expected cache hit rates, and cost assumptions.

If any of the above is off, call it out and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll loop Rafael and Ben in to get the workbook and the tech call on calendar.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call TCO recap & next steps (NovaHealth)

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary. A couple quick clarifications:

- Budget: yes, our POC cap is firm at $10k/month. If we can get a credible plan that fits inside that for the first 6 months, we’ll proceed to procurement.
- Traffic scenarios: please include estimates for both 1M prompts/mo and 5M prompts/mo in the workbook — we want a low- and high-volume view.
- ROI line: can you provide a 1–2 sentence executive summary that frames savings vs our current baseline?

Can you also confirm whether your batching/caching numbers assume any change to prompt length or model behavior (i.e., do we have to re-write prompts)?

Tom and I are available for the technical call next Wed/Thu afternoons PT. Procurement target: signed by end of June if numbers check out.

Appreciate it — Dana

Subject: Re: Post-call TCO recap & next steps (NovaHealth)

Hi Dana / Tom — quick preliminary numbers and assumptions (I’ll drop the workbook in the Drive link after sending):

Assumptions
- Avg tokens per request: 600 (input + output)
- Low scenario: 1M prompts/mo -> 600M tokens/mo
- High scenario: 5M prompts/mo -> 3B tokens/mo
- Baseline (no batching/cache/quant): current vendor effective cost used for comparison: $0.03 per 1k tokens (example)

Preliminary cost estimates
- Baseline cost (1M prompts / 600M tokens): ~$18,000/mo
- With Redwood (batching + KV cache hit ~35–50%): token-compute equivalent drops -> estimated cost: ~$8k–$11k/mo (1M prompts)
- High-volume economics (5M prompts): baseline ~$90k/mo -> with levers: ~$40k–$55k/mo
- Reserved capacity pricing: could push the above lower by another ~15–25% depending on commit and instance types.

Notes on integration / prompt changes
- In most cases batching and KV/prefix caching require minimal prompt rewrites; caching is most effective when you have repeated system messages or shared context.
- Rafael will validate latency impact and requirements for your SDK/agent integration.

Next actions
- I’ll upload the initial workbook now: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3C_TCO_workbook
- Rafael — can you propose 2 slots Wed or Thu afternoon PT for the tech deep-dive?

Ben
